title: Extra Floor
concept: A night-shift worker's elevator stops at floor 7½, a floor that doesn't exist on the panel.
setting: An old apartment block elevator and an identical-but-wrong corridor.
conflict: Theo needs to get home; the elevator only opens on 7½.
escalation: The corridor has his own apartment number, his own doormat, his own shoes outside — still wet from tonight's rain.
reveal: Floor 7½ is where his building keeps the version of him that didn't come home one night years ago.
ending: Back in the elevator, the panel now shows 7½ as a normal button. The real floor 8 is gone.
emotional_objective: Uncanny familiarity; the safe place made wrong.

hooks.line: My elevator stopped between the 7th and 8th floors. The doors opened anyway.
hooks.first_visual: Panel: a lit button between 7 and 8.

hooks.line: There's a floor in my building with my apartment on it. I don't live there.
hooks.first_visual: A door with the same number, a familiar doormat.

hooks.line: The floor sign just says: WELCOME BACK.
Why are my shoes outside a door I've never seen?
Someone on floor 7½ has been waiting for me to come home.

originality_review: Liminal-space genre convention (impossible floor) used generically; story beats, characters and reveal are original.
